title: The Verdicts
question: Which objects of scrutiny are judged almost only in the negative, and which criticism arrives with no way forward?

figures.title: Verdict mix per object, sorted by negativity
figures.deck: Positioning work — related work at 88% negative, novelty at 82% — is judged almost only in the negative.

claims.statement: The positioning objects — related work and novelty — are almost never written about except to criticise: 88% and 82% of their units are negative.
claims.derivation: summing all 410,586 2026 units by object: related_work is 9,033/10,306 = 87.65% negative, novelty is 9,409/11,440 = 82.25% negative

claims.statement: The share of units grounded in the reviewer's own explicit words is flat across all twelve objects (17–22%) — checked and retired from the chart rather than drawn.
claims.derivation: reviewer_explicit / n per object (obj_extras[o].reviewer_explicit / obj_extras[o].n), range across the twelve objects

figures.title: Criticism that arrives with no fix at all
figures.deck: 37% of novelty criticism offers no way forward — two to four times any other object.

claims.statement: Novelty criticism is also the least actionable, alone: 37% of it arrives with no fix, two to four times the no-fix share of any other object (8–18%).
claims.derivation: share of novelty's negative units lacking a suggested-fix field (1 − with_improvement/n), compared against 8–18% for the other eleven objects

caveats.text: "Comes with a fix" is a property of what the reviewer wrote, not of whether the problem is fixable — though for novelty the two are hard to separate: a reviewer who thinks a contribution too small often has no repair to offer.
